correctness.rationale: The statement has precisely quantified n>=3 and interprets components in the original selected-edge spanning graph. Domination iff <=1 isolated original vertex; a rooted-tree local pairing proves that every connected even-edge graph has an adjacent-edge edge partition; labeled-graph parity filter proves the generating function. The lower bound 3b>=n-1 comes from exactly three original vertices per matched adjacent edge pair, and constructed wedges attain equality for all residues. Defect delta=3r-v>=r-1 limits optimizer types to two-, four-, and six-edge components, giving exhaustive partitions and multinomial counts. Independent original-definition brute tests n=3..7 and minimum counts n=3..8 passed; finite checks are not used as infinite proofs.

value.rationale: Paired domination combines a global domination constraint and a perfect-matching condition; classifying all feasible sets on the natural Johnson/line graph J(n,2) reduces this nonlocal condition to a transparent even-edge connected-component rule. It determines an entire infinite polynomial family and every minimum placement, with four genuinely distinct optimizer profiles for n congruent 2 modulo 3, not merely a minor numerical bound. The associated square-root exponential identity relates complete graph edge-set enumerators to parity-filtered connected labeled graphs and can be reused in restricted component enumeration.
